Last Wednesday, I visited a Habitat for Humanity site build in Macon, GA. Over the past year and a half, the cost of living has skyrocketed. It is not just more expensive to put food on the table or fill the gas tank, it is also harder to buy or rent a home. Gutting the workers at USDA that help our farmers as well as chaotic tariffs and an unauthorized war in Iran have driving up the cost of fuel, disrupted crucial supply chains for everything from the food we eat to the materials we use to build housing.

While I continue to work hard in Congress to rein that in, I was glad to work with Democrats and Republicans this summer to pass the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act which will help improve the housing supply and prevent large corporations from scooping up chunks of property that make it harder for hardworking Americans to afford a home.

I continue working with municipal and county governments as well as community organizations to direct federal funds to local projects that help develop housing right here in Middle and Southwest Georgia so that it is a more affordable place to live, work, and raise a family.
